label: rejected

evidence.V1: Front and three-quarter read instantly as a wall with a mullioned window; centred opening; slab silhouette appropriate for a module.
evidence.V2: Clear: wall slab, medium window frame/sill/cap/plinth, small mullion cross and gold keystone.
evidence.V3: Window is small for an 8x12 panel and sits over a blank dark apron; proportions stiff.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on stones, frame, sill and keystone; sill close-up shows clean bevel catching light.
evidence.V5: Window, sill and end-section close-ups clean; no seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone greys, light frame, timber mullions, gold keystone; glass a muted blue-grey - still disciplined.
evidence.V7: 664 tris vs module target 800 - under target.
evidence.V8: Kit materials and accents used correctly, but the plain dark apron under the sill breaks the coursed stonework and the blue glass is outside the listed palette.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Box (or Default) collision, CanTouch off, Color white, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes.

evidence.V1: Front view reads as a window wall by colour (blue pane, cross muntin), but the silhouette is a solid slab with no opening - from the outline the window is invisible.
evidence.V2: Big wall, medium stone courses / frame / sill / plinth, small muntins and gold keystone - clear tiers.
evidence.V3: Stones are chunky and stylised, but the window is a small plain box frame and a large blank recessed panel sits under the sill with no stones, which reads unfinished/stiff.
evidence.V4: Stones, cap and sill are chamfered and catch light, but the muntins and keystone are razor-edged boxes (window_studio close-up) - inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Window, sill and end-section close-ups show clean shading; no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone hue plus timber muntins plus blue glass plus gold: one hue more than the main + one secondary limit.
evidence.V8: White vertex-colour material and stone/timber/gold kit colours match, but the blue glass hue and unchamfered muntins/keystone are minor mismatches with the kit spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box (or Default), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling pass (iou 0.98).

evidence.V1: Window reads only from the front/three-quarter; the silhouette is a solid rectangular slab (window not punched through) and the top view is a featureless bar.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: slab and cap ledge (big), block coursing, window frame and sill (medium), gold keystone and cross mullions (small).
evidence.V3: Clean but stiff: evenly sized rectangular blocks on a flat slab, no stagger, taper or irregularity; partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Consistent small chamfers on every block, frame, sill and cap ledge that catch light in the window and sill close-ups.
evidence.V5: Close-ups of window, sill and end section show clean flat shading, no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone grey in about 3 values, gold keystone, timber mullions and slate-blue glass; colourways (brick, sandstone) keep the same value structure.
evidence.V7: 664 tris vs module target 800, under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and kit chamfers, but the end section is a plain undressed dark slab face and the dark empty apron panel under the sill reads unfinished compared with the dressed face.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a modular piece (anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, white colour, grid-corner pivot); T1 tiling pass with iou 0.978.

artifacts: Large featureless dark panel under the sill
none visible; end faces are untextured plain slab (style, not an artifact)
top_fixes: Enlarge the window (taller opening) and course stones under the sill instead of the blank apron
Tint glass toward the kit steel grey or ink
Add a slightly deeper reveal/lintel stone above the frame for weight
Fill the blank under-sill panel with stone courses (or a proper apron) so the face reads finished
Chamfer the muntins and keystone to match the stone bevel
Consider an open (or darker, see-through-looking) window so the opening reads in silhouette, and fold the glass colour into the kit palette
Punch the window opening (or deepen the reveal) so the silhouette and three-quarter read as a window, not a slab
Fill or detail the empty recessed panel under the sill (apron blocks or a corbel) and dress the end section with block returns so ends look finished when tiled
Add slight block size variation/stagger and a stronger sill/lintel projection for a more stylised read
